codeReview.summary: Implementation correctly adds first-come-first-serve duplicate allele handling to YamlRef._normalize_and_verify_yaml(). The approach is sound: cross-provider duplicates are detected via pandas groupby, the DataFrame is deduped with drop_duplicates(keep='first'), and the raw YAML dict is updated in-place via _deduplicate_yaml_data() to keep self.yaml consistent. Tests are well-structured with 5 cases covering all three VAL-DUP contract items plus logging and mixed scenarios. All tests use small controlled YAML fixtures as required.

issues.description: Duplicate logging is emitted in two places: once in _normalize_and_verify_yaml() (per unique gene name) and again in _deduplicate_yaml_data() (per occurrence). For a single duplicate allele like IGHV1-2*02, at least 2 debug messages are logged. This is redundant but harmless since both are at DEBUG level.

Edge case: if a YAML has both same-source duplicates AND cross-provider duplicates simultaneously, the check `len(duplicated['source'].unique()) == 1` would be False, causing the code to silently deduplicate everything including the same-source duplicates (which should raise ValueError). This is a pre-existing design limitation in the if/else branching structure, not introduced by this change. Extremely unlikely in practice since YAML configs are either auto-generated or carefully hand-written.

VAL-DUP-002 contract says to verify by 'checking the sequence content of the resolved allele matches the first provider's sequence.' The test verifies the source field instead (entry['source'] == 'ogrdb'). This is actually a stronger and more direct verification since it checks provenance directly rather than comparing sequences. Acceptable deviation from the contract wording.
